documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 54.
Interval: no ED visits or new problems. Swallowing good. Still drinking daily. Busy summer at the warehouse.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20. All via mail order now.
Exam: weight up to about 103 kg. BP per flowsheet. Normal cardiopulmonary exam. Abdomen soft. Feet: sensation intact, no lesions. PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 9.
Health maintenance: colonoscopy 2021 normal (next 2031). Shingrix done. PCV20 done. Tdap 2019. Flu today. COVID per pt at a pharmacy this fall.
Plan: CMP and A1c today. Continue meds. Follow up in the winter for diabetes.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth daily until stone passes, up to 4 weeks
Dissolve 1 tablet on the tongue every 8 hours as needed for nausea
Take 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain, max 6 tablets per day

reports.text: Renal ultrasound. Indication: left flank pain, history of stone. Right kidney 11.4 cm, normal echotexture, no hydronephrosis, no stone. Left kidney 11.7 cm, normal echotexture, no hydronephrosis. A 6 mm echogenic focus with posterior shadowing is seen in the left ureter. Bladder partially distended, unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: 6 mm stone in the left ureter. No hydronephrosis.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Patient: Darren Upton  DOB 07/10/1971  Arrival 10/02/2025 19:40

HPI: 54 y/o man with prior kidney stone, presenting with two days of left flank pain. Sharp, comes in waves, wraps into the left groin. Nauseated, has not vomited. No fever, no burning with urination, urine looks normal to him.
PMH per patient: diabetes, high blood pressure, gout, achalasia, prior stone.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: T 36.8, HR 88, BP 135/85, SpO2 98%. BMI 32. Uncomfortable, shifting on the stretcher. Left CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft, nontender anteriorly. No rebound.

Results: UA pH 5.0 with uric acid crystals. Serum uric acid 8.6 mg/dL (high). Creatinine and potassium normal. WBC normal.
Renal US: 6 mm stone in the left ureter, no hydronephrosis.

ED course: ketorolac 15 mg IV and ondansetron 4 mg IV with good relief. Tolerating fluids. Repeat vitals normal.

MDM: left ureteral stone, 6 mm, with an acid urine and uric acid crystals — likely a radiolucent uric acid stone. Afebrile, pain controlled, normal renal function, no hydronephrosis: appropriate for outpatient passage trial.

Disposition: discharged 00:30. Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily up to 4 weeks, ondansetron ODT as needed, acetaminophen as needed. Strain urine and save any stone. Urology follow-up in 1-2 weeks, sooner for fever, uncontrolled pain or vomiting.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Was in the ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI I was in the ER last night for a kidney stone on the left side, 6 mm they said. They gave me a shot and sent me home with tamsulosin and nausea pills. Supposed to see urology. Pain is a 3 now.

documents.title: RE: Was in the ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know — we haven't received anything from the ED yet, I've asked for the records. Drink plenty of water, take the tamsulosin daily, and use the strainer. If you get a fever, can't keep fluids down, or the pain gets out of control, go back. Let's do a quick video check in about two weeks if it hasn't passed sooner.

documents.title: ED records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Records request faxed to the hospital ED for visit 10/02/2025.

documents.title: Passed it
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Pretty sure I passed the stone this morning, felt it go and the pain is totally gone. Didn't catch it in the strainer though, sorry. I'm going to cancel the urology appointment if that's ok.

documents.title: RE: Passed it
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. That's fine for now — we'll talk at the video visit Thursday about whether you still need urology.

documents.title: Video Visit — kidney stone
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, patient at work in a break room, identity verified.
Passed the stone on 10/11, not retrieved. No pain since, no fever, urine clear, no nausea. Finished with the nausea tablets. Still has a few tamsulosin left.
ED records not yet received; per pt, 6 mm left ureteral stone on ultrasound.
A/P: Left ureteral stone, passed. Stop tamsulosin. Keep fluids up, at least 2-3 liters a day. He cancelled urology; reasonable since it passed and he's pain-free. Will review the ED record when it arrives.

documents.body:

orders.reason: Acute right great toe pain and swelling, history of gout

documents.title: Toe pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pt texted at 6:40 am, called him back. Woke up during the night with the right big toe throbbing; red, swollen, can't stand the sheet on it. No injury. No fever. Remembers the one gout attack years ago, says this is worse.
Likely gout flare. He'd like to see someone who can sort out the gout long-term. Called the rheumatology group; they can see him tomorrow morning. Until then ice, elevate, acetaminophen. Go to urgent care or ED for fever, spreading redness, or if he can't bear weight at all.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets now, then 1 tablet in 1 hour; then 1 tablet twice daily until the flare resolves

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY — NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 03/26/2026
Patient: Darren Upton, 54 M. Referred urgently by PCP.

HPI: Right great toe pain, redness and swelling for two days. Came on abruptly overnight; throbbing; can barely put a shoe on. On questioning, he has had several smaller episodes over roughly the past two years in the same area that went away within a few days without treatment; he didn't mention them to anyone. Remote first flare years ago. Past history also of a ureteral stone last fall (uric acid crystals in the urine) and an earlier kidney stone.
Other history: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, achalasia treated with dilation, alcohol use disorder.
Medications: lisinopril, metformin, atorvastatin 20 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with gout and type 2 diabetes; mother with hypertension; paternal uncle with alcohol use disorder.
Social: beer daily, which he acknowledges. Never smoker.

Exam: BMI 32. Afebrile. Right first metatarsophalangeal joint red, warm and exquisitely tender with swelling. No other joints involved. No tophi.

Labs today: serum uric acid 9.2 mg/dL (ref 3.4-7.0), CRP 24 mg/L (ref <5). CBC, creatinine and glucose normal.

Assessment: acute gout flare, right first MTP (podagra), on a background of recurrent flares and uric acid nephrolithiasis.

Plan:
1. Colchicine: 1.2 mg now, 0.6 mg one hour later, then 0.6 mg twice daily until the flare settles.
2. Return in about 6 weeks once quiet to begin urate-lowering therapy with flare prophylaxis.
3. Reduce beer intake — discussed as a major flare trigger.

Rheumatology

documents.title: Rheumatology note received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rheum consult from 3/26 finally in. Gout flare R 1st MTP, uric acid 9.2, CRP 24. Colchicine short course. Plans urate-lowering after the flare. Pt replied by text the toe settled within about 5 days. Follow-up with rheum is 5/7.

medications.reason: Gout flare prophylaxis while starting allopurinol

documents.title: New gout medicines
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the rheumatologist yesterday. Toe is fine now. She started me on allopurinol 100 mg once a day and colchicine one pill a day for about 6 months so I don't flare while it kicks in. Wants a uric acid level in about 6 weeks, can I do that at your office?

documents.title: RE: New gout medicines
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Yes — we've added allopurinol and colchicine to your medication list. Lab can draw the uric acid any weekday morning around the third week of June; we'll send the result to rheumatology.
